units.source_text: 一般都是小姐过来叫我。

en.t: Usually it was the young lady who came to call me.

units.source_text: 小姐有时拐过檐廊拐角，站在我房门外叫我，有时穿过茶室，从隔壁房间的拉门后面现身。

en.t: Sometimes the young lady would turn the corner of the veranda and stand outside my room to call me, and sometimes she would pass through the tea room and appear from behind the sliding door of the next room.

units.source_text: 每次小姐走到门外，都会停下来，然后叫一声我的名字，问一句‘在学习吗？’

en.t: Whenever she came to my door, she would stop, call my name, and ask, "Are you studying?"

units.source_text: 我大抵在桌上摊开一本深奥的书，在专心研读，所以，在旁人看来，俨然在刻苦用功。

en.t: I usually had some difficult book open on my desk and was bent over it, so to anyone watching I must have looked as if I were studying hard.

units.source_text: 其实，我并没有特别专心研读，眼睛虽然盯着书，心里却似乎在等着小姐来喊。

en.t: In truth, I was not especially absorbed in reading; though my eyes were fixed on the book, my heart seemed to be waiting for the young lady to come and call me.

units.source_text: 若等不来小姐，我只好站起身，走到小姐的房间外面，这回轮到我问她：‘在学习吗？’

en.t: If she did not come, I had no choice but to get up and go outside her room, and then it was my turn to ask her, "Are you studying?"

units.source_text: 小姐的房间挨着茶室，有六叠大小。

en.t: The young lady's room adjoined the tea room and was six tatami mats in size.

units.source_text: 夫人有时候待在茶室，有时候待在小姐房间里。

en.t: Sometimes the mistress was in the tea room, and sometimes she was in the young lady's room.

units.source_text: 即是说，这两个房间虽有隔扇，也跟没有差不多，母女俩你来我去的，不分彼此。

en.t: In other words, although there was a partition between the two rooms, it was almost as if there were none, and mother and daughter went back and forth between them without drawing any clear distinction.

units.source_text: 我在拉门外一叫门，回应‘请进’的大多是夫人，小姐即便在里面，也没有答应过。

en.t: When I called from outside the sliding door, it was usually the mistress who answered, "Come in"; even when the young lady was inside, she never replied.
